body:
I resolve/attack the remaining product forks as follows:
- Do not silently redefine applicant's '발화 후 5초' to STT-final receipt. Release metric starts at annotated semantic audio endpoint -> eligible Console render; STT-final receipt -> render is diagnostic. This also fixes the report's contradiction of including 0.7s STT in a clock said to start after finalization. End-to-end p95 only; summing component p95 allocations is not proof.
- Define 'related' for release as claim-supporting or Q&A-actionable with direct source grounding, not merely topical; expert labels before execution.
- Human approval wins over ambiguous p7-9 because p10 is an explicit downstream gate; `SUPPORTED` only means eligible.
- Curated-only is first demo, not final MVP. Guarded pilot with private live recommendations proves latency/usefulness but full contract remains blocked until live eligible candidates can traverse an approval path to public output; publication can remain feature-flagged outside supervised pilot.
- Strict no-private-pixel implies private Console on a separate physical device for both mirror and extend. A browser topology callback cannot preempt an OS Duplicate transition.
- Dynamic public cards cannot honestly support 'anytime retract' while Stage is offline. Recommend connected retract/tombstone p95<=500ms; on WSS loss Stage immediately hides LIVE_VERIFIED cards (curated cards may remain policy-bound), shows degraded state, and never resurrects. Short local expiry is defense in depth.
- Claim-class policy: medical/legal/financial and other high-impact claims excluded from live public MVP; numeric/date/entity errors are critical-zero class.
Challenge especially the immediate-hide-on-disconnect choice and audio-end clock; I want no unresolved semantics.
